stage: blind-parallel A — every state in which the batch stands still although workable points exist

entries.defect: DEFECT: nothing DEFERS a point that will not converge. The queue order is fixed and the head point is taken by every successor in turn, so one stuck point stands the whole batch still — although the user's order names deferral ('indem stattdessen mit einem anderen Task weiter gemacht wird') as the primary alternative to stopping. FINAL STATE: a point that has failed to converge over a named threshold is marked deferred with its reason, drops out of head position, and the next workable point is taken without a human.

DEFECT: the launcher spawns the owner session with a cwd inherited from an existing point worktree, so the board bookkeeping splits between checkouts and the session dies of the inconsistency (measured 26.08.2026, point 944). CONDITION: any worktree exists and the launcher resolves cwd from anything but the main checkout.

DEFECT: the delegate-protection rule reads a live delegate's ordinary branch progress as a foreign live writer and refuses resurrection while the owner is dead. CONDITION: the refusal persists exactly as long as the delegate keeps working — which is precisely when workable work exists. FINAL STATE: a dead owner beside a live delegate is ADOPTED, never a reason to refuse.

DEFECT: the runaway watchdog counts a REFUSED start as 'started without progress', so an attempt that never began is charged to the failure budget and pulls the pause at three; when the pause expires the identical loop runs again, forever. FINAL STATE: only a real start attempt is counted, and a repeating refusal escalates outward instead of into a pause.

DEFECT: while the idle now-card stands, every state-changing call is refused, and the documented way out (board.mjs closing <N>) writes a NUMBERED card that the now-projection deletes in the same operation — so for a just-ticked point the refusal has no exit at all (point 937, reproduced three times).

DEFECT: the board step runs BEFORE the cleanup step and fails on a focus naming the point its own tick just closed, so the merge completes while branch, remote branch and worktree stay standing and the session is wedged behind the board guard. FINAL STATE: cleanup precedes the board step, or the board step tolerates the point it has just closed.

DEFECT: a CI run that concluded failure with a job that never STARTED (conclusion null, zero steps) is unclassified, so the guard hard-blocks the turn end on a red that no in-repo retry can reach — point 711's retry lives inside the job's steps and a job that never started has none. Only a human re-run clears it (point 953).

DEFECT: the verify tier stops at test-types, so ONE red type-check on main blocks every point's suites simultaneously, and there is no path that defers the blocked points and proceeds with work that does not need the tier (point 948). CONDITION: any commit reaching main with a red early tier stage.

DEFECT: the gate's second documented way out is a ledger row that no command in scripts/ writes, so an honestly-filed refusal stays blocked unless a human hand-appends JSON to a tracked ledger (point 942). CLASS: a documented exit with no command that can take it is a permanent stop wearing the mask of a choice.

DEFECT: the guard blocks the turn end unless a verified advancing condition holds. If the other guards simultaneously block the actions that would PRODUCE that condition, the session can neither act nor stop, and the deadlock carries no timer and no outward signal. FINAL STATE: an unresolvable block is a reportable event, never a silent hold.

DEFECT: a lock left by a process that died without releasing it makes the SessionStart hook tell every successor to STAND DOWN. CONDITION: liveness judged from the lock file rather than from the process, so no session is willing to work while no session is working.

DEFECT: the gate blocks the turn end while a committed render change lacks a covering run per backend; on a host where one backend cannot run at all the condition is UNREACHABLE and only a hand-written --defer clears it. FINAL STATE: an unreachable backend is classified as environment and recorded as such, not waited on forever.

DEFECT: publish refuses while any open point lacks a queue card, and board-first-guard refuses every mutation while the board is behind — so appending a new point blocks BOTH the board and the work until the cards happen to be written in the right order. CONDITION: measured this session on points 948-953; recoverable by hand, but the shape is a mutual block.

PARTLY INSURMOUNTABLE: a serving model outside the recorded chain stops the batch by design, and that is an acceptable stop only while the chain is genuinely unreachable. DEFECT: nothing distinguishes 'unreachable' from 'briefly failing', so a transient provider error takes the same permanent path as an exhausted quota.

DEFECT: the three-lane cap combined with the rule that tightly-coupled points must not run in parallel can exclude every remaining queue head, so the pool idles while points are open and nothing names which point may proceed. FINAL STATE: the exclusion set is computed and the first NON-excluded point is named, or the idleness is reported as a stop.

DEFECT: the boundary is committed as the last repository action and the successor is requested through the same protected start decision; if that request fails silently, nothing recovers but the 900-second OS tick — which the design itself calls the watchdog rather than the transport. FINAL STATE: a failed successor request is itself an event, not an absence.

DEFECT: a finding that cannot be filed — carrier unwritable, or the guard demanding a work-order write while the board guard blocks writes — blocks the turn end with no alternative durable sink. FINAL STATE: the finding always has a writable sink, and filing never depends on a mechanism that can be blocked.

DEFECT: the bounded responder wakes only when there is no live owner and no honored claim, so an owner that is LIVE but permanently wedged suppresses the one path that could report the standstill outward. CONDITION: liveness and progress are conflated; a wedged owner is alive by every probe.

DEFECT: a pending claim holds the launcher back for the claim's full lifetime; a claim taken in a window that is then left unattended stands the batch still while no work happens in the claiming window either. FINAL STATE: a claim that shows no activity is withdrawn by the mechanism, not by a remembered rule.

DEFECT: a declaration expires when its evidence stops advancing, but a declaration whose evidence keeps advancing while the WORK is dead — a log written by an unrelated process, a branch advanced by another session — holds the lease and suppresses the successor indefinitely. CONDITION: advancement is measured on the artefact, not on the declared work.

DEFECT: a user-set pause is an acceptable stop by construction, but an automatic runaway pause is stored the same way and inherits the same immunity, so a machine-set stop cannot be told from a human-set one. FINAL STATE: an automatic pause carries its own expiry and its own escalation; only a human pause is indefinite.

DEFECT: a landing can remove a worktree underneath a running delegate, after which every call in that delegate is refused and its uncommitted work is unrecoverable; the owner receives no signal distinguishing a strand that died from one that finished (measured 11.08.2026). FINAL STATE: a worktree with a live process is never removed, and its removal is refused with the pid named.

DEFECT: the written failure-mode table lists mechanisms INDIVIDUALLY and has no composition section, so a pair that only wedges in combination — the 944/945 pair being the proof — has no place to be recorded and no review that would find it. FINAL STATE: the inventory carries a pairwise composition check and this sweep's result.
